name: The Fairmont Chateau Lake Louise
positioning: Fairmont Chateau Lake Louise, a historic chateau-style hotel in Alberta's Banff National Park with a thermal bathing facility
best_for: Travelers who want a lake and mountain base in Banff National Park
Guests who want a thermal wellness experience during their stay

facts.text: The hotel is in Alberta's Banff National Park, a UNESCO World Heritage Site.
The property began in 1890 as a small log cabin opened by Canadian Pacific Railway president William Van Horne for tourists arriving by train.
BASIN Glacial Waters is a self-guided thermal experience at the hotel.
Louiza is a Mediterranean-inspired restaurant at the hotel.
Afternoon Tea is served at Fairview Restaurant.
The Alpine Social serves comfort food and craft beers.
Lakeview guest rooms have views of Lake Louise and Victoria Glacier.
In summer, guests can canoe on Lake Louise.
The hotel has programming for kids.
The on-site spa offers massage, body, face and nail salon services.

highlights.text: BASIN Glacial Waters has cold plunges, steam rooms and indoor-outdoor thermal pools.
In cold weather the lake freezes over and becomes an ice-skating rink.
The Fairview's dinner menu includes butcher's cuts, with locally sourced bison filet and elk striploin.
Fairmont Gold guests have a private concierge, an exclusive lounge and complimentary breakfast.

considerations.text: Parking at the hotel is available for an additional fee.
The hotel charges a Resort Experience Fee per room per night in addition to the room rate.
WhataHotel notes the remote mountain location requires travel planning for airport transfers.
